Note that plugging in $x=1$ gives the indeterminate form $\frac{0}{0}:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to 1}\frac{y(x)-2}{\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi x)} & =\frac{2-2}{\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi )} \\  & =\frac{0}{0}\end{aligned}
$$

However, we can use L'Hopital's rule to find this limit, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to 1}\frac{y(x)-2}{\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi x)} & ={lim}_{x\to 1}\frac{[y(x)-2]^{′}}{[\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi x)]^{′}} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to 1}\frac{{y}^{′}(x)}{\pi \operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi x)} \\  & =\frac{{y}^{′}(1)}{\pi \operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi )} \\  & =\frac{1\cdot (y(2))^{2}}{-\pi } \\  & =-\frac{1\cdot {2}^{2}}{\pi } \\  & =-\frac{4}{\pi }\end{aligned}
$$
